newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks recoup some losses by midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks recoup some losses by midday.

text.p: Wall Street shares pushed off session lows by midday on Monday, shrugging off some of the concerns about higher interest rates and inflation which were still dogging the bond market.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which slid shortly after the open as the bond market weakened further, pared losses to trade down around 14 points at 8179.
The Nasdaq composite was sturdy, gaining about eight points to 1602.
But the long bond, which sank Friday when robust July jobs and National Association of Purchasing Management data revived rate fears, lost 14/32 to yield 6.48 percent.

"The bond market has been weak the last two days but the stock market doesn't want to quit," Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt, said. "Nasdaq is strong and there is still a lot of momentum on the buy side."
Technology, transport and small-capitalization shares firmed while stocks in financial, utility, banking and insurance sectors declined.
